program: MSc in Music and Acoustic Engineering
qualification: Laurea Magistrale (Master of Science) — 2nd cycle, 120 CFU
accreditationStatus: REAL DEGREE. Italian state university laurea magistrale, MUR-accredited (class LM-32/LM-29 area). Confirmed on polimi.it official programme page.
language: English (100% — entire programme taught in English)
whatYouStudy: Sound and acoustic engineering with an interdisciplinary approach integrating information engineering, acoustics, signal processing, computer engineering and music technologies. Theoretical and applied acoustics, digital audio, sound signal processing, music technologies, multimedia systems. NOTE: this is an ENGINEERING degree, not a studio-craft degree — no record-production/mixing/mastering studio track is advertised.
entryRequirements: Verbatim (polimi.it): applicants need 'an adequate background in information and industrial engineering disciplines, in particular in computer engineering, electronics, telecommunications, mathematics, and physics.' Non-Italian degrees must be 'recognised as equivalent in level, nature, and academic content to an Italian degree.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES — emphatically. This is the one programme in the territory that REWARDS a computer-science/software-engineering BSc. No music qualification is required or requested. Quote: 'an adequate background in information and industrial engineering disciplines, in particular in computer engineering...'
portfolioSpec: NONE. No portfolio, no tracks, no audio submission. Selection is on academic transcript + CV + motivation via the Politecnico online application.
auditionSpec: NONE — no performance audition and no practical production test. Purely documentary academic evaluation by the Admission Committee.
tuitionNonEU: Approx. €3,898.20/yr for non-EEA students (top band). UNVERIFIED against the current official fee table — the polimi.it fees page did not resolve; figure comes from secondary aggregator sources. Politecnico applies ISEE/ISEEU-parificato banding, so the real figure can fall well below this.
otherFees: Regional right-to-study tax approx. €140/yr + €16 stamp duty. UNVERIFIED for 2027/28.
totalCostEstimate: Tuition approx. €3,900/yr worst case; Milano living costs approx. €900–1,200/month. Approx. €15,000–18,000/yr all-in without funding.
scholarshipName: Politecnico di Milano Merit-Based Scholarship for International Students; Bando Benefici DSU (Politecnico administers its own DSU bando)
scholarships: 1) PoliMi Merit-Based Scholarship for international students — full tuition-fee waiver, may include accommodation/living funds. 2) Regional/institutional DSU right-to-study grant — 2026/27 MUR minimum €7,171.11/yr for a fuori sede student, ISEE ceiling €26,306.25. Bando published at polimi.it/fileadmin/.../Bando_Benefici_DSU_2026-2027.pdf.
languageRequirement: English only. No Italian required for the degree.
englishTest: English proficiency certificate required (IELTS/TOEFL or PoliMi's own test). Exact minimum band UNVERIFIED for 2027 entry.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE reference: PoliMi runs multiple non-EU rounds from roughly October to spring for the following September. Exact 2027/28 dates UNVERIFIED.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE: typically opens October of the preceding year. UNVERIFIED for 2027/28.
fitNote: Best structural fit in the whole territory for THIS candidate's academic background, and the only one where no music portfolio exists to block him. But it will NOT teach him to make records — it is DSP/acoustics engineering.

institution: Conservatorio di Musica 'Giorgio Federico Ghedini' di Cuneo — Scuola di Musica Elettronica (METS)
program: Tecnico del Suono — Ingegneria del Suono e Multimedia (DCSL61)
qualification: Diploma Accademico di II livello (120 CFA)
accreditationStatus: REAL DEGREE. Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello, MUR/AFAM ministerial code DCSL61, equivalent to laurea magistrale. Confirmed on metscuneo.it study-plans page.
englishTeaching: No — no English-taught teaching found. UNVERIFIED whether any module is in English.
whatYouStudy: Sound engineering and multimedia: recording, mixing and finalisation of multitrack material, foley and video sonorisation, sound technique projects, electroacoustics, multimedia audio. Production/technical rather than compositional (the compositional strand is the separate DCSL34).
entryRequirements: Verbatim (metscuneo.it): access requires possession of 'Diploma Accademico di I livello, di Laurea di I livello o di Diploma di Conservatorio vecchio ordinamento.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES, on the face of the text — 'Laurea di I livello' (any first-cycle university degree) is listed as sufficient, which covers a BSc Software Engineering. Crucially the exam structure explicitly caters to candidates WITHOUT a music first-level diploma: only holders of an I-level diploma in Sound Engineering or Electronic Music are EXEMPTED from the practical mixing test and from the second (theory) test — meaning non-music candidates are expected to sit both. So a non-music entrant is contemplated by design, but must pass music theory and ear training.
portfolioSpec: Verbatim requirement: candidates deliver to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it 'alcuni propri lavori (audio, multimediali, etc…) ed un curriculum vitae'. Materials must be supplied as permanent share links (Google Drive / Dropbox / OneDrive) with no expiry. NO fixed number of tracks and no length or format specification is given — 'alcuni' ('some') is all the page states.
auditionSpec: NOT a performance audition — a PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST plus oral. First test: (a) practical — mix and finalise a multitrack recording supplied by the conservatoire (waived for holders of a I-level diploma in Sound Engineering or Electronic Music); (b) oral — present an original foley/video sonorisation, present prior sound-technique projects, motivational interview. Second test (waived for I-level diploma holders): music theory and general musical culture across sight-singing/intonation/rhythm (COTP/06), ear training (CODM/04) and music history (CODM/05). Typically held early September.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as an exact figure. Italian state conservatoire contribution is ISEE-banded; a non-EU applicant resident abroad who does not file an ISEEU parificato is placed in the TOP band. Typical AFAM top band is roughly €1,500–2,000/yr; with an ISEEU parificato below threshold it falls to €0–450 plus the regional tax.
otherFees: Admission exam fee (small, order of €30–50) + €72.67 government tax + regional right-to-study tax (€130–160). UNVERIFIED exact 2027/28 figures.
totalCostEstimate: Approx. €1,700–2,300/yr fees worst case in year one; Cuneo living cost is low for Italy, approx. €600–800/month.
scholarshipName: EDISU Piemonte — Borsa di studio DSU
scholarships: EDISU Piemonte regional right-to-study grant covers AFAM conservatoire students. 2026/27 MUR minimum for a fuori sede student €7,171.11/yr, ISEE ceiling €26,306.25 / ISPE €57,187.53 (DD n. 175/2026). Non-EU freshmen with family not resident in Italy are ranked in a separate graduatoria and students from 'Paesi particolarmente poveri' file a certificate from the Italian diplomatic representation instead of income documents.
languageRequirement: Italian. Non-EU applicants via the Universitaly pre-enrolment route must normally demonstrate Italian at B2 (or pass the institution's Italian test). UNVERIFIED for this specific conservatoire.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: admission exams held early September; portfolio and CV to be received 'entro la data dell'esame di ammissione'. No fixed published cut-off date. 2027/28 dates UNVERIFIED.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE: typically spring (roughly April–July) for a September exam. UNVERIFIED.
fitNote: One of the most candidate-friendly entries found: explicitly accepts a generic Laurea di I livello, the portfolio spec is loose ('some of your own works'), and the gate is a mixing test he could train for. Blocker: everything is in Italian and there is a music-theory/ear-training exam.

qualification: Diploma Accademico di II livello (120 CFA)

englishTeaching: No. UNVERIFIED whether any module is in English.
whatYouStudy: Per the DCSL61 ministerial declaratoria: competencies in the use of equipment and technologies for sound — sound recording, television and radio production; electroacoustic and computer instrumentation; history of electroacoustic and computer technologies applied to music. Exit profiles named in the ordinamento: production assistant, sound editor, sound technician, theatrical sound technician, sound archives, electronic music publishing.

institution: Conservatorio di Musica 'Nino Rota' di Monopoli
qualification: Diploma Accademico di II livello (120 CFA)
accreditationStatus: REAL DEGREE (AFAM II level) — but CONDITIONAL ACTIVATION. The conservatoire's own 2026/2027 admissions page states the Tecnico del Suono course is activated only if a minimum of 4 students enrol.
englishTeaching: No — but note the conservatoire assesses incoming foreign students in BOTH Italian and English.
whatYouStudy: Sound technique / studio and live audio production under the Nuove Tecnologie department. Detailed syllabus UNVERIFIED.
entryRequirements: Verbatim in substance (conservatoriodimonopoli.org): students must hold 'an academic diploma of first level, or university degree, or previous-order diploma combined with secondary school certificate' or an equivalent foreign qualification aligned with the chosen programme.
acceptsNonMusic: LIKELY — 'or university degree' is listed as an access title without a subject restriction, subject to the 'aligned with the chosen programme' coherence test. Quote: 'accademic diploma of first level, or university degree, or previous-order diploma combined with secondary school certificate ... or equivalent foreign qualifications aligned with the chosen program.'
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — no portfolio specification published on the admissions page.
auditionSpec: Two components: an instrumental/practical exam plus theoretical assessments whose content varies by course; for Nuove Tecnologie department courses the theoretical content was still 'under definition' on the page. ADDITIONALLY, and importantly for this candidate: 'All foreign students must complete Italian and English language assessments,' plus mandatory music theory evaluation in rhythm, harmony and related areas — waived only for holders of an Italian secondary diploma or AFAM credentials.
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED. Puglia is among the cheapest regions — living costs approx. €500–700/month.
